uncertainties.detail: Identity confidence is 68. The authoritative record supplies a name, Chinese geography and a specific yacht; HKEX supplies a highly plausible exact-name wealthy investor. No independent source connects those two evidence clusters, so the record remains below the required score of 85.

The upstream fields store Lyu as first name and Wenyang as last name, while Chinese convention and HKEX usage may indicate Lyu is the surname and Wenyang the given name. Searches covered Lyu Wenyang, Wenyang Lyu, Lu Wenyang, Wenyang Lu and Chinese-character candidates; none established authoritative segmentation or the yacht link.

Primary HKEX filings conclusively describe a Mr Lyu Wenyang who controls LVYY holding vehicles, held a disclosed 9.16 percent Kingwisoft interest and later participated in another financing. The filings do not publish nationality, residence, date of birth, image or vessel ownership, leaving collision risk unresolved.

The authoritative 40.05-metre and 338-GT specification matches YachtBuyer's 2018 Sunseeker 131 formerly named Angelus. A different 40.05-metre, 341-GT yacht built in 2019 is marketed as The Boat of Fate 2; it was excluded from identity reasoning.

AIS sources place the UK-flagged 40-metre Fate 2 on the China coast and around Hong Kong. That is consistent with the authoritative China residence and Hong Kong investment candidate, but a vessel's location is not proof of its beneficial owner.

The exact-name candidate appears to be an investor with controlled holding companies, but public filings begin after capital has already been accumulated and do not explain its origin. Even if the identity were later bridged, wealth origin would remain Unknown unless stronger evidence emerges.

No official LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, birth information or biography was attributable to the yacht owner. Search results for academics, US company managers and other Wenyang Lyu or Lu profiles were excluded as unbridged namesakes.
